chunks: Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said:

Whoever sells a commodity and says, 'Its price is such-and-such hand to hand, and its price is such-and-such on deferred payment, so take it at whichever price you wish and make its sale one transaction.'
Then he said: 'He is entitled only to the lesser of the two, even if it was deferred.'

key_terms.أَقَلُّهُمَا: the lesser of the two prices
key_terms.سِلْعَةً: a commodity or item being sold
key_terms.صَفْقَتَهَا: its sale contract or commercial bargain

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a seller gives one price for cash and another for credit in a single sale?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a sale in which two prices are proposed, one for immediate payment and one for deferred payment, without firmly settling one price at the time of contract. It states that the seller is only entitled to the lower of the two amounts, even if the payment is deferred, emphasizing clarity and fairness in commercial transactions.
